full_judgment:
Bijan Kumar Das J: This petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 9-9-1993 passed by the Subordinate Judge, Moulvibazar in Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 directing the appellant-petitioner to deposit half of the decretal dues or in lieu thereof Bank Guarantee by 23-9-1993. 

 3. The present appellant then filed Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for restoration of the suit upon setting aside the ex parte decree on the ground that the appellant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing in Court when the suit was called on for ex parte hearing. The trial Court by the impugned order dated 9-9-1993 directed the appellant-petitioner to deposit half of the decretal dues or Bank Guarantee by 23-9-1993. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocates and perused the impugned order and all other connected papers. The suit for recovery of loan money was filed before the Artha Rin Adalat on 21-5-1991 and the suit was decreed ex parte against the defendants on 19-2-1992. The present petitioner who was defendant No. 3, filed Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 on 1-4-1992 and the impugned order was passed on 9-9-1993. It appears that the impugned order was passed in view of the amendment made in Artha Rin Adalat Ain which came into force on 17-7-1992. By the said amendment, Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was made available to a judgment debtor on deposit of half of the decretal dues or furnishing Bank Guarantee of the said amount. The trial Court appears to have passed the order on the basis of the amended Artha Rin Adalat Ain overlooking that Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 was filed prior the amendment came into force. Artha Rin Adalat Ain 1990 provided only one appeal before the High Court Division against the judgment and decree passed ex parte or on contest on deposit of half of the decretal dues furnishing Bank Guarantee. There was no provision for filing a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the original Artha Rin Adalat Ain. When the Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 was filed under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure on 1-4-1992 there was no such provision for filing a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The trial Court therefore committed a gross error of law in failing to notice that the Miscellaneous case filed under Order IX rule 13 was not entertainable at the relevant time against an ex parte decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat in Artha Rin suit for recovery of loan money. Mr Md Mahbub Ali, the learned Advocate for the appellant candidly referred to a decision in the case of MAC Proprietor Mahtabuddin Chowdhury and another vs Agrani Bank Thatari Branch Dhaka reported in 47 DLR 233 where a Division Bench in a similar case took a view that an aggrieved party i.e. a judgment debtor, has only the forum of appeal when a decree is passed either on contest or ex parte. Provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure are applicable subject to this special law. In the said decision a Division Bench considered sub-sections (4) and (5) of section 5 of Artha Rin Adalat Ain and section 7(1) and (2) of the said Ain and held—"This Artha Rin Adalat Ain is a special law under which courts were constituted which has its own forum of appeal. So, by way of interpreting the provisions of sub-sections (4) and (5) of section 5 it cannot be found that this is an ordinary Civil Court for all practical purposes and all the provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure are applicable in the proceeding . The provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure are applicable subject to the provisions of this special law. In the said decision a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed before the Artha Rin Adalat which dismissed the said case on the finding that the summons of the suit was duly served. The aforesaid case under Order IX rule 13 arose out of an ex parte decree passed in a title suit for realisation of some money. The Division Bench in the said case ultimately held that Miscellaneous case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not available to the judgment debtor at the relevant time. This Division Bench decision completely covers the facts of the present case before us. The judgment and decree passed ex parte on 19-2-1992 could be set aside by filing a Miscellaneous Case under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure as Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not available at the relevant time to the judgment debtor. In such facts Miscellaneous Case No. 7 of 1992 filed under Order IX rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was not entertainable and accordingly, the present appeal is not maintainable
